questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a permanent wind?

__
 
• Permanent winds are those that persist throughout the year and are associated with the Earth's atmospheric circulation system. 
 
• They help to distribute heat, moisture, and air masses across the planet, playing a crucial role in shaping global climate patterns.

​**Loo**__

__
 
• **Loo **is not type of permanent wind.
 
• It is a strong, dry and hot afternoon wind from the west in the summer, blowing over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India and Pakistan.
 
• It is particularly strong in the months of May and June.
 
• Exposure to it also leads to lethal heat strokes because of its extremely high temperatures (45 °C–50 °C or 115 °F-120 °F).
 
• The technical words that signify the direction in which the wind is blowing are 'Windward' and 'leeward.'
 
• The direction upwind from the point of reference is windward.
 
• Loo has extended its reach and has now gripped more parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and even West Madhya Pradesh. Moreover, some parts of this region are also reeling under heat wave conditions.

• Westerlies: These winds blow from the southwest in the Northern Hemisphere and the northwest in the Southern Hemisphere, generally found between latitudes 30° and 60° in both hemispheres.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere is suitable and most important to humans?

__
 
• Troposphere: Average height is 13 km.

 
 
• The air we breathe exists here.
 
• This layer contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• All changes in climate and weather take place in this layer. 
 
• Almost all the weather phenomena like clouds, rainfall, fog and hailstorm occur in this layer. 
 
• This is the most important layer for all biological activity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Stratosphere: up to an altitude of 50 km from the earth’s surface.

 
 
• Almost free from clouds, most ideal for flying aeroplanes, Contains a layer of ozone gas (Ozonosphere).
 
• Temperature increases with height in this layer.
 
 
 
• Mesosphere: Up to an altitude of 80 km. Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from the space.
 
 
• Temperature decreases with height in this layer.
 
 
 
• Thermosphere: It extends between 80-400 km. In the thermosphere, the temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
 
• The ionosphere is a part of this layer. It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is known as the ionosphere. 
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission.
 
• The International Space Station and satellites orbit in this layer. Temperature increases with height in this layer.
 
 
 
• Exosphere: The uppermost layer of the atmosphere is known as an exosphere.
 
 
• This layer has very thin air. Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the stratosphere?

options.text: It extends up to a height of 50 km.
It contains a layer of ozone gas.
This layer is almost free from clouds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The statement "It lies above the mesosphere" **is incorrect when referring to the stratosphere.
 
• The stratosphere is actually located above the troposphere, which is the lowest layer of the **Earth's atmosphere.**
 
• The stratosphere extends from about 10 to 50 kilometers (6 to 31 miles) above the Earth's surface. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Earth's atmosphere is divided into five primary layers based on temperature changes with increasing altitude. **From the bottom to the top, these layers are:

 
 
• **Troposphere:** This is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, extending from the Earth's surface up to an average altitude of about 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) at the poles and 18 kilometers (11 miles) at the equator. The troposphere is where weather phenomena occur, and it contains most of the Earth's air mass and moisture.
 
• **Stratosphere: **Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere, extending from the top of the troposphere up to approximately 50 kilometers (31 miles) in altitude. The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which plays a crucial role in absorbing the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
 
• **Mesosphere: **The mesosphere is situated above the stratosphere and extends up to around 85 kilometers (53 miles) in altitude. In this layer, temperatures decrease with increasing altitude, reaching extremely low temperatures.
 
• **Thermosphere: **The thermosphere starts above the mesosphere and extends upward to about 600 kilometers (373 miles). It is characterized by a significant increase in temperature due to the absorption of intense solar radiation. Despite the high temperatures, the thermosphere would not feel hot to human perception due to its extremely low density of particles.
 
• **Exosphere:** The exosphere is the outermost layer of the Earth's atmosphere. It begins around 600 kilometers (373 miles) above the Earth's surface and extends indefinitely into space. The exosphere consists of extremely sparse gas molecules that gradually dissipate into the vacuum of outer space.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding air pressure?

options.text: High pressure is associated with cloudy skies and wet weather.
Low pressure is associated with clear and sunny skies.
The air always moves from high pressure areas to low pressure areas.
The air pressure is lowest at sea level and increases with height.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The air always moves from high pressure areas to low pressure areas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

 
• ​The **air always moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas.**
 
• This i**s because air always moves along pressure gradients, from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, in an attempt to equalize the pressure.**
 
• This movement of air is what we experience as wind.

***Hence statement 3 is correct.***

 
• **High pressure** is generally associated with** clear skies and calm weather, not cloudy and wet weather.**
 
• This is** because high pressure involves air sinking toward the surface of the earth,** which** inhibits cloud formation.**

*Hence statement 1 is incorrect.*

 
• Conversely, l**ow pressure is often associated with cloudy skies and wet weather, not clear and sunny skies.**
 
• Low pressure involves **air rising from the earth's surface, which can lead to cloud formation and precipitation.**

*Hence statement 2 is incorrect.*

 
• The air pressure is **highest at sea level and decreases with height.**
 
• This is due to the** weight of the air above compressing the air at lower levels (like sea level), making it denser and therefore exerting more pressure.**
 
• As you go higher, **there's less air above you, so the pressure decreases.**
 
• **For this reason, it is difficult to breathe in the hilly areas and mountains.**

*Hence statement 4 is incorrect.*

questions.question: Which of the following countries belong to the polar regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The countries that belong to the polar regions are Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Alaska in the USA and the Siberian region of Russia.
 
• The polar region is the area around the North Pole or the South Pole. The northern polar region consists mainly of floating and pack ice, 7–10 feet (2–3 m) thick, floating on the Arctic Ocean and surrounded by land masses.
 
• Polar regions are covered with snow and it is very cold for the most part of the year. Sun does not set at the pole for six months and the sun does not rise for the other six months. Temperature goes as low as -37 degrees C in winter.
 
• The Polar Bear, Caribou, Snowy Owl, Arctic Hare, Arctic Fox, Narwhal, Walrus, Musk ox and Beluga Whale are some of the animals which live in the Arctic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Both the Arctic (North Pole) and the Antarctic (South Pole) are very cold because they get very little direct sunlight. The Sun is always low on the horizon, even in the middle of summer. In winter, the Sun is so far below the horizon that it doesn't come up at all for months at a time.
 
• Since the weather is so so cold, there are not very many animals that live in these polar climates. Animals that do live in these areas have adapted over the years to be able to survive in freezing temperatures, tons of snow, and strong, blowing winds.
 
• The most well-known animal that lives in polar climates is the polar bear, a huge mammal that has a thick layer of body fat and a fur coat that is water-repellent to protect it from the freezing waters.
 
• There are many things that threaten the polar region, but the biggest of these is climate change, which is when the temperature of the earth gets hotter. As the temperature of the earth continues to rise, the ice in the polar areas melts, which makes the land and coastlines get smaller.

questions.question: Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth’s oceans, caused by the uptake of ________ from the atmosphere.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Ocean Acidification:

 
 
• Oceans are an important reservoir of CO2, absorbing a significant quantity of it (one-third) produced by anthropogenic activities and effectively buffering climate change.
 
• Ocean acidification is the change in ocean chemistry - lowering of ocean pH (i.e. increase in the concentration of hydrogen ions) driven by the uptake of carbon compounds by the ocean from the atmosphere.
 
• As the uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide by the ocean increases, the concentration of hydrogen ions in the ocean increases, the concentration of carbonate ions decreases, the pH of the oceans decreases and the oceans become less alkaline – this process is known as ocean acidification.
 
 
 
• Effects of Ocean Acidification:
 
 
• Oceans are an important reservoir of CO2, absorbing a significant quantity of it (one-third) produced by anthropogenic activities and effectively buffering climate change.
 
• The uptake of atmospheric carbon dioxide is occurring at a rate exceeding the natural buffering capacity of the oceans.
 
• Increasing acidity depresses metabolic rates and immune responses in some organisms.
 
• Seawater absorbs CO2 to produce carbonic acid, bicarbonate and carbonate ions.
 
• However, the increase in atmospheric CO2 levels leads to a decrease in pH level, an increase in the concentration of carbonic acid and bicarbonate ions, causing a decrease in the concentration of carbonate ions.

__
 
• ** The troposphere is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere**, extending from the surface up to an average altitude of about **7 to 12 kilometers (4.3 to 7.5 miles).**
 
• The height of the troposphere varies depending on the location, season, and weather conditions. However, the average height of the troposphere is about **11 kilometers (6.8 miles) above sea level**.

• **Earth's atmosphere** can be divided into **five primary layers **based on **their temperature and altitude**:

• **Stratosphere**: This layer lies above the troposphere, extending from about 12 to 50 kilometers (7.5 to 31 miles) in altitude. The ozone layer is located in this layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

questions.question: Jet streams are a particular form of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**geostrophic winds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jet streams** are a particular form of geostrophic winds.
 
• These are fast flowing, narrow air currents found in the atmospheres of some planets, including Earth.
 
• Jet streams are typically located near the altitude of the tropopause and are westerly winds (flowing west to east).
 
• They form at the boundaries of adjacent air masses with significant differences in temperature, such as the polar region and the warmer air to the south.
 
• The major jet streams on Earth are the polar jet streams and the subtropical jet streams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geostrophic winds** are winds that result from a balance between the Coriolis effect and the pressure gradient force.
 
• These winds flow parallel to the isobars (lines of constant pressure) and are important in the study of meteorology and climate.
 
• Understanding jet streams is crucial for weather forecasting, as they influence weather patterns and the development of storm systems.
 
• Commercial aviation also takes advantage of jet streams to reduce travel time and fuel consumption on certain routes.

questions.question: The variation between a high air temperature and a low temperature that occurs during the same day is called ______ temperature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diurnal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diurnal** temperature variation refers to the fluctuation between the highest and lowest temperatures that occur within a single day.
 
• Such variations are common in many parts of the world and are influenced by factors such as **altitude, latitude, and local weather patterns**.
 
• Diurnal temperature changes are more pronounced in **desert regions** due to the lack of moisture which prevents the air from retaining heat.
 
• Understanding diurnal temperature variation is important for agriculture, meteorology, and various environmental studies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annual Temperature Variation:**

 
 
• This refers to the changes in temperature that occur over the course of a year.
 
• It is influenced by factors such as **seasonal changes, earth's tilt, and orbit around the sun**.
 
• Annual variations are more significant in temperate regions compared to tropical regions.
 
 
 
• **Wet Bulb Temperature:**
 
 
• It measures the lowest temperature that can be reached by evaporating water into the air.
 
• It is important in understanding the effects of heat and humidity on humans and is used in calculating heat index.
 
 
 
• **Durian:**
 
 
• Durian is a large, spiky fruit known for its strong odor.
 
• It is unrelated to temperature variations and is often called the "king of fruits" in Southeast Asia.

• The ozone layer is **typically thicker over the poles than over the equator.**
 
• The ozone layer exists in **the stratosphere**, a layer **10 to 50 km above the Earth’s surface.**
 
• The reasons for ozone depletion are a wide range of** industrial and consumer applications, mainly refrigerators, air conditioners (hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs), chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)), and fire extinguishers.**

• The Negative Effects of the ozone hole are certain types of **skin cancers, eye cataracts, and immune deficiency disorders.**
 
 
• **UV rays also affect plant growth, reducing agricultural productivity.**
 
 
 
• The international community established the **Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances in 1987**, to address the destruction of the ozone layer.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Ozone layer is indeed found in the **stratosphere**, which is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, just above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons **(CFCs) are responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer, leading to the formation of the **ozone hole**.
 
• The ozone layer is located approximately **15-30 km above the Earth's surface**, which helps protect living organisms by filtering out harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
 
• Statement 4 is incorrect because recent studies have shown that the** ozone layer is slowly recovering due to the global reduction in the use of CFCs** and other ozone-depleting substances, primarily due to the Montreal Protocol.

• CFCs are man-made chemical compounds that were commonly used in air conditioning, refrigeration, and as propellants in aerosol sprays.

• It was agreed upon on **September 16, 1987**, and has been ratified by all 197 UN member countries, making it one of the most successful environmental agreements in history.
 
• Thanks to the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer is expected to recover to 1980 levels by the middle of the 21st century.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**
 
 
• The stratosphere is the second layer of the Earth's atmosphere, situated above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• It extends from about **10 km to 50 km **above the Earth's surface.
 
• The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation.

questions.question: During October — November, the apparent movement of sun is towards the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** apparent movement** of the **sun **during** October and November** is towards the** South.**
 
• This is because during these months, the **Earth is tilted away from the sun** in the **Northern Hemisphere **and **towards the sun** in the **Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• As a result, the sun appears to move towards the South, and the **days become shorter** in the Northern Hemisphere and** longer** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the **winter solstice** and occurs around** December 21st **in the Northern Hemisphere and** June 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **movement of the sun** is caused by the** Earth's rotation on its axis **and its **revolution **around the sun.
 
• The Earth's axis is tilted at an** angle of 23.5 degrees **relative to its orbit around the sun, which** causes the seasons.**
 
• During the **winter solstice**, the tilt of the Earth's axis is at its **maximum,** causing the** least amount of daylight** in the Northern Hemisphere and the **most amount of daylight** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The opposite occurs during the **summer solstice,** which happens around** June 21st** in the Northern Hemisphere and** December 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• During the **equinoxes**, which occur around **March 20th and September 22nd, **the tilt of the Earth's axis is perpendicular to the sun, causing **equal amounts of daylight and darkness** all over the world.

questions.question: What is the name of the cold phase of the ENSO climate pattern that describes the unusual cooling of the surface waters of the region?

__
 
• **La Nina** is the cold phase of the ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) climate pattern.
 
• It describes the unusual cooling of the surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
 
• La Nina events typically bring about a variety of weather changes, including increased rainfall in some regions and drought in others.
 
• This phenomenon is the opposite of El Niño, which is the warm phase of the ENSO climate pattern.
 
• La Nina can influence global weather patterns and has significant impacts on agriculture, water supply, and hurricane activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ENSO cycle includes both El Niño and La Nina phases, as well as periods of neutral conditions.
 
• La Nina events are characterized by stronger-than-average trade winds, which push warm water towards the western Pacific, allowing cold water to upwell in the eastern Pacific.
 
• The cooling effect of La Nina can last for several months and typically occurs every 2 to 7 years.
 
• La Nina can also influence the Atlantic hurricane season, often leading to more active hurricane periods.
 
• Scientists monitor the ENSO cycle using various tools, including satellite observations and ocean buoys, to predict and understand its impacts.

questions.question: Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?

__
 
• **El Nino** is a phenomenon that leads to **weakening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• During El Nino, the** sea surface temperatures** in the Pacific Ocean near the Equator become **warmer **than usual, which affects the** atmospheric circulation **and leads to weakening of trade winds.
 
• Trade winds are the **prevailing easterly winds** that blow towards the **Equator in the tropics**, and they are important for **navigation and weather patterns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coriolis force **is a phenomenon that influences the** direction of winds and ocean currents**, but it does not directly lead to weakening of trade winds.
 
• **Mango Shower** is a **meteorological phenomenon** that occurs in some parts of India during the **pre-monsoon season**, and it is not related to trade winds. 
 
• **La Nina** is a phenomenon that is opposite to **El Nino,** and it leads to **strengthening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• Hence, the statement "Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?" is **correctly answered** by option 3, El Nino.
